questions.question_text: Describe the main manifestations of engineering in ancient times and in the medieval period.
questions.model_answer: In ancient times, engineering manifestations included: 1) Architecture and construction (pyramids, temples, obelisks, cities, castles, palaces using stone and brick); 2) Water management and irrigation (canals, channels, reservoirs, water-lifting devices, dams for the Nile); 3) Civil engineering (roads, bridges, city planning, public facilities, ports); 4) Mechanical engineering (wheels, pulleys, levers, simple machines for lifting and moving loads); 5) Astronomical engineering (astronomical calculations for time and seasons, structures aligned with the sun and stars); 6) Military engineering (fortresses, walls, war and defense machines). In the medieval period, engineering manifestations included: 1) Architecture and structures (mosques, churches, palaces, castles, Islamic architecture with arches, domes, minarets); 2) Water engineering (canals, irrigation systems, water wheels and norias, water distribution within cities); 3) Mechanical engineering (water mills, windmills, gears, mechanical machines); 4) Civil engineering (bridges, roads, sanitation systems, castles, fortifications, walls); 5) Marine engineering (shipbuilding, navigation, astronomical instruments for direction and location); 6) Development of science and engineering in Islamic civilization (contributions to mathematics, astronomy, mechanics, engineering, medicine; water machines, clocks, mechanical devices; scholars such as Al-Jazari, Al-Khwarizmi, Ibn al-Haytham, and Al-Biruni).

questions.question_text: Explain the main characteristics of modern engineering and the steps a modern engineer follows to solve a problem.
questions.model_answer: The main characteristics of modern engineering include: 1) Reliance on science and mathematics (mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science, materials science, statistics). 2) Use of technology and computers (CAD, CAM, CAE, simulation, AI, machine learning, digital twin, data analysis). 3) Problem solving (using knowledge to reach practical solutions). 4) Achieving a balance between performance, safety, quality, and cost effectiveness. 5) Attention to safety (ensuring systems are safe to use). 6) Attention to the environment and sustainability (reducing energy consumption, using renewable energy, reducing pollution, recycling, reducing waste, designing sustainable products). The steps a modern engineer follows are: 1) Identify the problem or need. 2) Analyze the problem using mathematics, physics, science, and computers, and study alternatives. 3) Design by converting the idea into an engineering design using design, simulation, and modeling programs. 4) Implementation by converting the design into a real product, system, or facility. 5) Testing and evaluation to ensure the design works correctly and safely and to measure performance against specifications. 6) Improvement and development to reduce cost, increase efficiency, improve quality and safety, and reduce energy and material consumption.

questions.model_answer: A modern engineer should possess: 1) Scientific knowledge (mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering sciences) to understand and analyze problems. 2) Analytical thinking to break down problems into parts. 3) Problem-solving ability to reach practical and innovative solutions. 4) Creativity and innovation to develop new solutions rather than repeating traditional ones. 5) Use of computers and technology (programming, CAD, simulation, AI, data analysis) to design and analyze efficiently. 6) Communication skills to communicate with engineers, technicians, managers, clients, and researchers. 7) Teamwork because modern engineering projects are usually carried out by integrated teams. 8) Professional ethics because engineers are responsible for decisions that may affect human life, the safety of structures, the environment, and the economy, so they must have honesty and professional responsibility.

questions.question_text: Explain the meaning of technology, its linguistic origins, and its main goals.
questions.model_answer: Technology is the use of scientific and practical knowledge, skills, tools, machines, and systems to develop solutions that help humans solve problems, meet needs, and accomplish tasks more efficiently, quickly, and accurately. The word 'Technology' comes from Greek roots: Techne means art, skill, craft, or the way of mastering work, and Logos means science, knowledge, or study. Therefore, technology is associated with knowledge and skill related to applying, making, and using things in a practical way. Technology is not just devices; it includes knowledge, skills, methods, tools, machines, software, processes, systems, and ways of working. The main goals of technology are: 1) Saving time. 2) Increasing speed. 3) Increasing accuracy. 4) Increasing productivity. 5) Reducing cost. 6) Improving product quality. 7) Improving safety. 8) Facilitating human life.

questions.question_text: Explain the relationship between science, engineering, and technology using a concrete example such as the development of a mobile phone.
questions.model_answer: The relationship can be summarized as: Science discovers → Engineering designs → Technology applies → Society benefits. Using a mobile phone as an example: Science studies electricity, electromagnetic waves, semiconductors, and physics. Engineering uses this science to design electronic circuits, the processor, the antenna, the communication system, and the battery. Technology assembles this knowledge and these designs into smartphone technology. Finally, society uses the phone for communication, internet, photography, education, and work. Thus, science discovers the underlying principles, engineering designs practical solutions, technology applies them into usable products and systems, and society benefits from the final application.
